rationale: Record test-only coverage for the materialized runtime's canvas behavior-owner cascade, plus the two realm hazards it exposed. The materialized runtime entry resolves which behavior node owns each live canvas through an ancestor walk for pointer handlers, a gesture-channel ownership set, a full-gesture tiebreak, and a geometric containment fallback with an ambiguity guard, then binds through two deliberately asymmetric paths: __pulpBindMaterializedCanvases__ throws on a missing visual anchor or a refused native bind, while the post-commit refresh records readiness instead. None of that was reachable from a test, because the existing commit-cost case evaluates the same generated entry with empty canvasBindings and behaviorCanvasAnchors, so every canvas clause was dead code during the run and its counters read zero, which is indistinguishable from a perfect score. This adds a dependency-free node --test file that evaluates the shipped generator output with non-empty bindings and stubs bindCanvasBehaviorAt and getLayoutRect, and documents in the import-design skill that the entry gates its callback registry on instanceof Map (so the Map must be constructed inside the sandbox) and that arrays it returns cross realms. Every case was break-confirmed by hand against the generator with a green control. No generator, importer, DesignIR, packaging, or shipped output behaviour changes: the two changed paths are a new test file and a skill document, so this touches no accepted expansion boundary and no Vellum source authority, and the disposition is watch-only.
